wire.headline: Energy firm reports revenue growth alongside job cuts and plant closures
sentences: Revenue rose by 7% year on year to 4.26bn GBP for the quarter ending 30 September.
Pre-tax profit fell by 12% to 310m GBP during the same period.
The company announced plans to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
Two gas plants, one located in Wales and another in Kent, are scheduled to close by March 2027.
CEO Marian Holt stated that cost pressure has been sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend was held steady at 12.4p per share.
Shares dropped by 4.2% during morning trading.

PD.headline: Energy firm announces 850 job cuts as cost pressures mount

sentences.text: For the quarter ending 30 September, Revenue increased year on year by 7% to 4.26bn GBP.
The company is set to make 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
CEO Marian Holt stated that the cost pressure is sharper than expected.
A Kestrel Securities analyst noted that these job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
The union Unite plans to ballot members on taking industrial action.
The MP for Deeside has asked for an urgent meeting with the company.
The company confirmed that customer bills will remain unchanged until April 2027.
The council leader is seeking assurances regarding the Kent plant.
